items.notes: Lemma 9.15 POVM-via-block-encoding. Verified against primary Eq.(9.58)-(9.62): W block-diagonal gives W|u>|0^a>|psi>=(1/(beta sqrt(2^m))) sum_i |i>|0^a>sqrt(P_i)|psi>+|perp>; postselection on 0^a kills |perp> (each (<0^a|tensorI)|perp_i>=0); orthonormality of |i> removes cross terms; sum_i||sqrt(P_i)|psi>||^2=sum_i<psi|P_i|psi> uses sqrt(P_i)^dag sqrt(P_i)=P_i (PSD root, correct); completeness sum_i P_i=I collapses to <psi|psi>=1 giving P(succ)=1/(beta^2 2^m), matching Eq.(9.62). Assumptions (shared a, shared beta, uniform PREP, normalized psi) are the real load-bearing hypotheses. Sound. Distinct from parent generic A/alpha postselection cores (be-007, plan-006) and from Chapter-2 POVM item plan-001 (different source/result).

Lemma 9.15 continuation, verified vs Eq.(9.63)-(9.66): normalization of sum_i|i>sqrt(P_i)|psi>=1 by orthonormality+completeness (Eq.9.64); P(i|succ)=<psi|P_i|psi> (Eq.9.65); collapsed state sqrt(P_i)|psi>/sqrt(<psi|P_i|psi>) (Eq.9.66); pure->mixed lift by linearity to rho->sqrt(P_i)rho sqrt(P_i)/Tr(P_i rho) matching update rule Eq.(9.51); unconditional P(i)=(1/(beta^2 2^m))<psi|P_i|psi> chains 201 correctly. All steps correct and faithful. Distinct result from 201 (output statistics/update vs scalar success probability).

Verified vs Eq.(9.57)/(9.67): naive repetition cost 1/P(succ)=beta^2 2^m (exponential in m); good amplitude sqrt(p); amplitude amplification rotates angle theta (sin^2 theta=p) to pi/2 in O(1/theta)=O(1/sqrt(p))=O(beta 2^{m/2}) rounds, each one W and one W^dag; O(log(1/delta)) outer repetitions; total O(beta 2^{m/2} log(1/delta)), matching Eq.(9.57). Quadratic-speedup angle argument correct, not merely quoted. Distinct from 201: 201 derives the probability, 203 derives query complexity/amplification; rubric grades 1/sqrt(p) scaling + log factor, not the probability itself, so no restatement of the same relation.

Example 9.14 impossibility (counterexample). Verified numerically for c in {0.3,0.6i,0.8}: PSD zero-expectation forces E_psi=a|phi_perp><phi_perp|, E_phi=b|psi_perp><psi_perp|; <psi|phi_perp>=sqrt(1-|c|^2) gives a=b=1/(1-|c|^2); Tr(E_psi+E_phi)=2/(1-|c|^2)>2=Tr(I) for 0<|c|<1 (checked: 2.198, 3.125, 5.556) so no two-element unambiguous POVM; adding P_?=I-P_psi-P_phi with weights 1/(1+|c|) restores a valid POVM. Impossibility argument genuine and correct. Distinct core from 205 (necessity-of-inconclusive vs validity-of-construction; different arguments). Parent-fixed metadata only: step2 supporting_nodes now includes concept:matrix-analysis (the step already used the <psi|phi_perp> computation); content/Q/A unchanged, no math impact.

Example 9.14 validity (proof). Verified numerically: (ii) sum=I by definition of P_?; (iii) <phi|phi_perp>=0 and <psi|psi_perp>=0 (~1e-16) giving unambiguity <phi|P_psi|phi>=<psi|P_phi|psi>=0; P_psi,P_phi PSD as nonneg scalings of rank-1 projectors; S=P_psi+P_phi has eigenvalues {1,(1-|c|)/(1+|c|)} so ||S||=1 and P_?=I-S has eigenvalues {0,2|c|/(1+|c|)}>=0 (confirmed e.g. c=0.8 -> {0,0.889}). All PSD checks correct. Distinct from 204.

Boundary / hypothesis-diagnosis on Lemma 9.15. Verified: (a) distinct beta_i -> postselection yields (1/sqrt(2^m)) sum_i (1/beta_i)|i>sqrt(P_i)|psi>, statistics prop to (1/beta_i^2)<psi|P_i|psi>, i.e. effective family {P_i/beta_i^2} need not sum to I, so the completeness collapse that produced 1/(beta^2 2^m) genuinely breaks - correct. (b) per-branch ancillas a_i -> no single |0^a><0^a| projector flags success across all branches, so (I tensor <0^a| tensor I)|perp>=0 fails - correct. Minimal fixes (pad to common beta / non-uniform PREP; shared ancilla a=max a_i) are sound. Both named assumptions are indeed load-bearing. Accurate.

items.notes: Example 9.16, verified vs Eq.(9.70)-(9.71): O'_A loads |theta~_ij>; CR gives (cos(pi theta~)|0>+sin(pi theta~)|1>)|theta~> with sin>=0 on range and A~_ij=cos(pi theta~); (O'_A)^{-1} depends only on unchanged (i,j), acts as identity on the ancilla, so it uncomputes |theta~> coherently across both ancilla branches. Decoherence/which-path argument correct: discarding the entangled work register would leave a marker that kills (i,j)-branch interference downstream, so the final inverse query is mandatory - matches source emphasis on uncomputation. Faithful, original phrasing.

Boundary, Section 9.6 Eq.(9.68). COORDINATOR SKEPTICISM (false 'strict <1 necessary' / |A_ij|=1 degenerate) CHECKED AND RESOLVED in the final MAIN artifact: reference answer, rubric r1-r2, steps and native_nl now state the amplitude A_ij|0>+sqrt(1-|A_ij|^2)|1> is a valid normalized state iff |A_ij|<=1, with |A_ij|=1 explicitly LEGITIMATE (only the sqrt term vanishes), impossibility restricted to |A_ij|>1, and ||A||_max<1 called a sufficient convenience/numerical margin, NOT a necessity. Regime analysis is now mathematically correct and does not overclaim necessity. Preprocessing A->A/M with M>=||A||_max is correctly tied to subnormalization. Accept.

Concept, Section 9.6 / Example 9.16. Verified: bit oracle = digital/query interface (explicit readable string, fan-out/arithmetic); amplitude oracle = analog interface consumed by block encodings; conversion = arithmetic query + controlled rotation (irreducible digital->analog step) + inverse query (uncompute); reversibility forces counting both forward and inverse queries ('no free cleanup'); d-bit work register borrowed clean (returned to |0^d>), amplitude qubit persistent output. Resource accounting accurate and consistent with 207. Distinct facet (model comparison / cost roles) from 207 (construction) and 208 (normalization regime).

Example 9.17 (Eq.9.72-9.73). Core identity verified: U_A=O_A, <0|<i|U_A|0>|j>=A_jj<0|0><i|j>+sqrt(1-|A_jj|^2)<0|1><i|j>=A_ii delta_ij (since <0|1>=0), so U_A in BE_{1,1}(A); c(j)=j triviality (no O_c) correct. COORDINATOR SKEPTICISM (false global-optimality of alpha=1) CHECKED AND RESOLVED in the final MAIN artifact: question now asks whether alpha=1 is optimal 'for every diagonal A or only in a specific case'; reference answer, rubric r4, step4 and native_nl now state the lower bound alpha>=||A||=max_i|A_ii|, that alpha=1 saturates it iff ||A||=1, and for ||A||<1 a smaller alpha=||A|| is achievable (e.g. encoding A/||A||), so alpha=1 is the construction's value and NOT a global optimum when ||A||<1. The earlier false claim is removed; the corrected statement is mathematically correct. Accept.

Section 9.7 / Eq.(9.77)-(9.80). Verified: an s-regular bipartite graph has chromatic index s (Koenig line-coloring), so edges partition into s disjoint perfect matchings; each matching gives a bijection j->c(j,ell) packaged by O_c; A^{(ell)} supported on matching ell is 1-sparse with A=sum_ell A^{(ell)}; equal-weight LCU with D=H^{tensor s} has coefficient 1-norm s giving alpha=s=s||A||_max, consistent with ||A||<=s||A||_max (Lemma 2.46) and the floor alpha>=||A||. All claims correct; source attributes the matching decomposition to Koenig (Die25 Prop 5.3.1) exactly as cited. 'alpha=s natural' is correctly stated as the worst-case saturation, not a universal optimum (consistent with the 210 correction). Distinct core.

Proposition 9.19 / Eq.(9.81)-(9.84). Verified the inner-product propagation: D,O_A,O_c map |0>|0^s>|j> to (1/sqrt(s)) sum_ell (A_{c(j,ell),j}|0>+...|1>)|ell>|c(j,ell)>; Hermiticity of D propagates the target to (1/sqrt(s)) sum_{ell'}|0>|ell'>|i>; <0| kills the |1> branch, <ell'|ell>=delta collapses the double sum, <i|c(j,ell)>=delta selects the unique matching, yielding (1/s)A_ij (unique ell if A_ij!=0, else 0). Matches Eq.(9.84) exactly. Correct. Distinct from 211 (graph decomposition vs explicit matrix-element verification).

Proposition 9.22 / Fig. 9.8 / Eq.(9.88)-(9.92). Verified the two-oracle (O_r,O_c) model: D,O_c,O_A,SWAP on source and D,O_r on target give (1/s) sum_{ell,ell'} A_{c(j,ell),j} delta_{i,c(j,ell)} delta_{r(i,ell'),j}; the paired deltas enforce column-side routing c(j,ell)=i and row-side routing r(i,ell')=j; unique surviving term (1/s)A_ij for A_ij!=0, 0 otherwise. The explanation that arbitrary O_A rotations on zero entries are harmless (no (ell,ell') selects a non-pattern position) matches the source remark after Eq.(9.89). Matches Eq.(9.92). Correct. Distinct from 212 (single-oracle Oc vs dual Or/Oc model, BE_{s,n+1}).

Section 9.8 / Definition 9.23. Verified: the block-encoding definition fixes only the top-left ancilla-0^m block =A/alpha, leaving other blocks free up to global unitarity, so A=A^dag does not force U_A=U_A^dag - matches source statement that only the upper-left block is guaranteed Hermitian. Concrete example correct: amplitude-oracle encoding of a real diagonal entry a acts as rotation [[a,-sqrt(1-a^2)],[sqrt(1-a^2),a]], non-symmetric hence non-Hermitian though its (1,1) block is a. Definition 9.23 (U_A=U_A^dag, set HBE) correctly stated as strictly stronger. Qubitization motivation (reflection on 2D subspace, two-step closure, Chebyshev) is correct and consistent with item 220. Distinct boundary core.

Proposition 9.24 / Fig. 9.9 / Eq.(9.93)-(9.98). Verified the two-register symmetric propagation: ancilla <0| overlaps keep sqrt(A_{c(j,ell),j}) from ket and conjugate sqrt(A_{c(i,ell'),i})^* from bra; deltas delta_{i,c(j,ell)}, delta_{c(i,ell'),j} select the unique matched term (1/s) sqrt(A_ij) sqrt(A_ji)^*; Hermiticity A_ji=A_ij^* gives sqrt(A_ji)^* = (sqrt(|A_ij|)e^{-i theta/2})^* = sqrt(|A_ij|)e^{i theta/2} = sqrt(A_ij), so product = (sqrt(A_ij))^2 = A_ij, giving (1/s)A_ij and U_A in HBE_{s,n+2}(A). Matches Eq.(9.98); the exact point where Hermiticity recombines the two half-entries is correctly identified. SOURCE-FIDELITY NOTE: the primary text Eq.(9.95) writes sqrt(1-|A_ij|) (not sqrt(1-|A_ij|^2)) and the author faithfully reproduced this as written; the matrix-element derivation only uses the sqrt(A_ij)|0> branch so the result is unaffected either way. Correct. Distinct HBE core.

All linear-algebra steps correct and faithful to the subspace generalization. Distinct core.

Section 10.1 / Definitions 10.1-10.4 / Eq.(10.15)-(10.16). Verified: for Hermitian A=VDV^dag with SVD Sigma=|D|, W=V sign(D): odd f gives f^diamond(A)=V sign(D) f(|D|) V^dag and f(|lambda_i|)=sign(lambda_i) f(lambda_i) so sign(D)f(|D|)=f(D), giving f(A); even f gives f^triangleright(A)=V f(|D|) V^dag with f(|lambda_i|)=f(lambda_i)=f(D), giving f(A). The 'definite parity removes the |lambda| vs lambda sign ambiguity' explanation is correct and matches Eq.(10.15)-(10.16). Both cases handled correctly. Distinct core.

items.notes: Eq.(10.17)-(10.23). Verified numerically (A=[[1,2],[0,3]]): A~=[[0,A^dag],[A,0]] Hermitian; A~|0>|v_i>=sigma_i|1>|w_i>, A~|1>|w_i>=sigma_i|0>|v_i>, so A~|z_i^pm>=pm sigma_i|z_i^pm> (confirmed for both singular values 3.650, 0.822). Block expansion of f(A~) via f_even/f_odd into triangleright/diamond/triangleleft generalized functions is correct; even f -> f(A~)|0>|psi>=|0>f^triangleright(A)|psi>, odd f -> |1>f^diamond(A)|psi>, with deterministic ancilla outcome because definite parity zeroes one component. Matches Eq.(10.22)-(10.23). Correct. Distinct from 217 (Hermitian-A equivalence vs general-A dilation mechanism).

Section 10.1 (p.166), A^k not an SVT / inverse exception. Verified: A^2=W Sigma (V^dag W) Sigma V^dag exhibits an interior unitary M=V^dag W between two Sigma factors; the three SVT forms carry a single diagonal g(Sigma) with no interior unitary, so A^2 is not an SVT unless M is diagonal (normal/special case); A^{-1}=V Sigma^{-1} W^dag has the odd-SVT diamond form (f(x)=x^{-1}, f_SV(A^dag)=A^{-1}) with no cross term because inversion transforms a single Sigma factor. Structural obstruction argument correct and matches source discussion. Correct counterexample. Distinct core.

Section 10.2.1 / Eq.(10.25)-(10.41). Verified numerically (lambda=0.6): U_A Hermitian with U_A^2=I; applying U_A twice yields U_A|perp_i>=sqrt(1-lambda_i^2)|0^m>|v_i>-lambda_i|perp_i>, so H_i is 2D invariant with reflection matrix [[lambda,sqrt(1-lambda^2)],[sqrt(1-lambda^2),-lambda]]; [Z_Pi]=diag(1,-1); O=U_A Z_Pi = rotation [[lambda,-sqrt(1-lambda^2)],[sqrt(1-lambda^2),lambda]]; O^k top-left = T_k(lambda) (confirmed k=1,2,3,5 against cos(k arccos lambda)); summing over i gives O^k in BE_{1,m,0}(T_k(A)). The claim that Hermiticity (U_A^2=I, second application) is exactly what closes the 2D subspace is correct and correctly flagged. Matches Eq.(10.40)-(10.41). Correct. Distinct core; capstone of the qubitization chapter.
